QuestionStmt.S: A fair coin is tossed 99 times. If X is the number of times head occur then $P[X = r]$ is maximum when $r =$

Solution.S:
$$P(\text{getting head}) = p = \frac{1}{2}$$

$$\therefore q = 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Here, $n = 99$.

$$\therefore P(X = r) = {}^{99}C_r \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^r \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{99-r} = {}^{99}C_r \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{99}$$

For a binomial distribution, $P(X = r)$ is maximum when $r$ is the most probable value.

If $n$ is odd, the maximum value of ${}^nC_r$ occurs at $r = \frac{n-1}{2}$ and $r = \frac{n+1}{2}$.

$$\therefore r = \frac{99-1}{2} = 49 \quad \text{and} \quad r = \frac{99+1}{2} = 50$$

Among the given options, $r = 49$ is present. Hence the correct option is B: 49.
